summary: Buena Park sits barely five miles from the Disneyland Resort, yet its own economy is anchored by Knott's Berry Farm — one of the oldest theme parks in the United States, predating Disneyland by more than a decade — which, along with the surrounding Entertainment Corridor along Beach Boulevard, makes tourism and hospitality a genuine local employment engine rather than just a neighbor's industry. The terrain is flat coastal plain, no ridgelines or canyon drama, which means the city's 10.6 square miles at nearly 7,800 people per square mile pack tightly together in a grid of wide arterials and residential blocks bisected by the I-5 and SR-91 freeways; those highways are both commute lifelines to jobs across Orange and Los Angeles counties and the physical seams that chop the city into disconnected pockets. At a median household income of roughly $108,000 and a median home price near $772,000 — a ratio just above 7-to-1 — buying requires significant savings or dual incomes, while median rent around $2,112 stays within conventional affordability thresholds for that income level. Daily weather is remarkably steady: 76°F highs, 55°F lows, and over nine hours of sunshine year-round, which softens the fact that parkland is scattered and the streetscape leans commercial-corridor rather than tree-canopied stroll. Buena Park is a place where the entertainment industry literally operates inside city limits, yet daily life revolves around freeway on-ramps.
